supplement.where: Appendices A–I are included on PDF pp. 27–84. The preregistration documents are described as online; their URLs are replaced by 'URL removed to maintain anonymity' (pp. 41, 43, and 66).
supplement.holds: Appendices A–I are included on pp. 27–84. Tables A.1–A.2 give final analyzed arm counts (pp. 35–36); Table A.3 gives an intermediate logo sample labeled pre-filtering, not final analyzed or documented randomized counts (p. 37). Appendix C gives sample construction and exclusions (pp. 44–48); D defines scoring (pp. 49–52); E–F specify normalization, regression models and participant-clustered inference (pp. 53–59). Appendix F.2.1 supplies the Revised-versus-DALL-E-2 logo confidence interval (p. 58). Appendix H supplies DreamSim and Z-score robustness statistics (pp. 63–65), and I supplies additional preregistered image-replication analyses and deviations (pp. 66–84). The statistical appendices used here are all in this PDF.

paper_design_summary: Two preregistered online experiments randomly assigned US Prolific participants to DALL-E 2, DALL-E 3 with reduced prompt rewriting, or DALL-E 3 with default GPT-4 rewriting (pp. 8–9, 34, 40 and 43). Participants repeatedly prompted their assigned model to replicate a fixed target image or create an original logo from an open-ended brief; the resulting images were scored for target fidelity or LLM-judged logo quality, respectively (pp. 10–12 and 49–50). Researcher replay of the same prompts separated model and prompting effects; the logo experiment provides the eligible creativity evidence (pp. 11–13).

participants.exclusions: The raw dataset contained 2,059 participants; this is a raw-data count, not an explicit tally at random assignment. Removing blank prompts, invalid Prolific IDs and logging failures left 2,029 people; requiring at least 10 successful prompts left 1,914. Restriction to the first 10 prompts was not preregistered. Excluding participants who repeated the same prompt at least five times consecutively left 1,899; excluding incomplete surveys left 1,893. Further post-hoc removal of prompts with failed image generation/replay or duplicate attempt numbers affected 370 prompts. The final analyzed sample comprised 1,893 people and 18,560 prompts (pp. 45-46, Appendix C.4). Appendix E.3 separately reports 371 replay-affected prompts out of 18,990 (p. 54), whereas C.4 reports 370 total post-hoc exclusions after survey exclusions. Their denominators and descriptions differ; the document does not explain how the counts relate. The final people and prompt counts above are explicitly stated in C.4.

task.description: Iteratively prompt the assigned model to reproduce one randomly assigned target image as closely as possible. Fifteen targets covered business/marketing, graphic design, and architectural photography. This bounded target-matching task is retained in the study inventory but is not the open-ended creative task supporting core eligibility (pp. 8-11, sections 3-3.3).

outcomes.name: Expected image-replication fidelity to the assigned target
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: The paper-primary score is expected CLIP embedding cosine similarity to the assigned reference image, averaging 10 generated images per participant prompt (pp. 10–11, section 3.2.1). Higher similarity means better replication quality, not less diversity. Main-text analyses use post-hoc replay/regeneration of the original prompts to address model drift (pp. 13 and 45); this is not a later unassisted human test. The analysis unit is a participant-prompt's average output score. n_units is the full retained all-arm prompt count, not the number of generated images or the number of observations in each pairwise contrast (p. 46, Appendix C.4). Overall ATE regressions include attempt and target-image fixed effects, with standard errors clustered by participant (p. 55, Appendix F.1.1). DreamSim, inverted as 1 minus its original distance, is an alternative fidelity metric; Z-score and percentile rescalings, and first/average/best-attempt summaries are variants of the same outcome (pp. 49, 53–54, 63–64, 66, and 75–80). Reported Z-score effects use within-target/attempt scaling across arms rather than a participant-level control SD (pp. 53–54). Quantile coefficients refer to the distribution of fidelity, not semantic diversity (pp. 16–17 and 57–58). Fidelity is coded usefulness under the codebook's single-output quality category: the paper calls the averaged similarity an expected quality score (p. 11).
outcomes.delay: Human prompting occurred in the assisted task session. Main-text image scores use later researcher-generated replays/resamples of the same prompts; this is not a later unassisted participant test (p. 45, Appendix C.3).

task.description: Create the best original logo for a hypothetical organization from one randomly assigned brief. Fifteen briefs specified the organization, background, a few required visual elements, and intended uses, while allowing open-ended creative designs. There was no target image or uniquely optimal design (p. 11, section 3.3; p. 41, Appendix B.5.1-B.5.2).
task.duration: Up to 25 minutes to submit at least 10 prompts; analysis restricted to the first 10 prompts (p. 9, section 3.1; p. 41, Appendix B.5.1; p. 47, Appendix C.5).

outcomes.name: Logo design quality / fulfillment of the client's brief (Bradley–Terry strength)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: gpt-4.1-nano, temperature 0, judges which of two logos better fulfills the client's requirements; image order is randomized. A sampled 20% of within-brief pairings of original and replayed images supplies win–loss matrices, from which maximum-likelihood Bradley–Terry β strengths are estimated per image (pp. 11–12 and 49–50). The instruction assesses fit/quality, not an explicit novelty or overall-creativity rating. Although pairwise judgments generate the score, treatment-effect regressions use the resulting output-level scores with attempt and logo-task fixed effects and participant-clustered standard errors (pp. 58–59, Appendix F.2). n_units is the retained all-arm original prompt/output count, not the much larger number of scoring comparisons or an exact replay-expanded regression N (p. 47, Appendix C.5). No prompt-level repeated-generation averaging is used for logos (p. 12). Within-logo/attempt Z-score normalization and attempt trajectories are robustness variants of this outcome; the Z-score standardizer is across arms within task/attempt, not the participant-level control SD (pp. 53–54 and 64–65). Table 2 estimates distributional heterogeneity of quality, not cross-person content similarity. Human validation is mentioned but supplies no treatment-effect estimate (p. 12, footnote 9). The human validation used approximately 19,000 image pairs; neither the number of human evaluators nor a human-rated treatment-effect estimate is supplied (p. 12, footnote 9).
outcomes.delay: Participant outputs were produced during the AI-assisted session. Subsequent researcher replay and scoring do not constitute delayed unassisted creative work (pp. 12-13, sections 3.3.1-3.4; p. 45, Appendix C.3).

eligibility.reason: S2 independently meets all three criteria: individuals were randomly and blindly assigned to different generative-AI configurations (p. 9, section 3.1; p. 34, Appendix B.1); 1,857 people were analyzed across the arms (p. 47, Appendix C.5; p. 36, Table A.2); and their original logos were scored for fulfillment of open-ended client briefs using LLM judgments summarized as Bradley-Terry strengths, an output-quality/usefulness outcome on a creative design task (pp. 11-12, sections 3.3-3.3.1; pp. 49-50, Appendix D.2). All arms use AI, so the direct comparisons are ai_design. S1's fixed-reference fidelity task remains outside the eligible creativity estimates; routing its retained AI-available usefulness outcome to with_ai does not establish creative-task eligibility. No remaining open item affects these decisions.

one_line_finding: In the logo experiment (1,857 people analyzed; p. 47, Appendix C.5), DALL-E 3 (Verbatim) improved quality over DALL-E 2 by 0.8075 Bradley–Terry β (95% CI [0.7120, 0.9030], p < 10^−10; p. 18, section 4.2.1), with replay attributing approximately 92.7% to model capability and 7.2% to prompt adaptation (prompting p = 0.101; p. 19, section 4.2.2).
open_questions: Exact counts at assignment are not explicitly reported: 2,059 and 2,067 are recruited/raw-data counts, while 1,893 and 1,857 are analyzed counts. All n_randomized fields remain null (pp. 8, 40, 43 and 45–47).

Preregistration URLs are redacted, so the manuscript's preregistration claims can be recorded but an independent preregistered primary-outcome hierarchy cannot be checked (pp. 41, 43 and 66). Data and code are promised upon publication, without usable URLs (p. 8, footnote 4).
The human logo-validation exercise reports approximately 19,000 image pairs, not an evaluator count, and no human-rated treatment-effect estimate (p. 12, footnote 9).

The relation between C.4's 370 post-hoc prompt exclusions and E.3's 371 replay-affected prompts is unexplained. The passages use different descriptions and denominators; no common reconciled exclusion count can be confirmed. Final S1 counts remain the explicitly reported 1,893 people and 18,560 prompts (pp. 46 and 54).
notes: Final review read the complete markdown through Appendix I.2 and checked the retained numerical claims, eligibility facts, challenge passage, and unresolved questions against PDF page text. PDF and printed page numbers coincide. The paper reports 3,750 participants analyzed across the two experiments (p. 1; pp. 46-47); S2 alone supplies core creativity eligibility. Both screeners listed the same two outcomes. Both retained AI-available usefulness outcomes are routed to with_ai under the codebook question rule. S1 remains fixed-target replication context and is excluded from eligible creativity estimates; S2 supplies the eligible creative-task evidence (pp. 10-12; creativity-codebook.md, section 1). Prompt length, parts of speech, successive prompt similarity, within-person prompt dispersion and strategic shifts describe inputs or interaction strategies, not creativity of the final images or diversity across different people's outputs (pp. 50–52). Tables 1–2 concern the distribution of quality, not content homogenization. DreamSim, rescalings, attempt trajectories and first/average/best performance summaries remain variants of the same output measures (pp. 63–84), not additional studies or constructs. The GPT-4V exercise in Appendix I.H8 calibrates target difficulty and does not supply another randomized human study. There is no after_ai participant test; later researcher replay reuses prompts from assisted sessions. Replay contrasts are retained separately with comparison_type other and are not additional randomized arms or independent samples. For direct DALL-E 3 configuration comparisons, Verbatim is the tested modification and Revised is the default, following codebook section 5 and PDF p. 38; reported percentages remain explicitly in the original Revised-relative-to-Verbatim orientation. No effect sizes, standard errors, reversed percentages or arm differences were computed. Quantile-model coefficients and SEs are labeled separately from average effects; their presence in statistics_available does not imply a numeric SE was printed for the overall ATE. Reported Z-scores use the paper's within-task/attempt standardization, not a new participant-level standardized mean difference. n_units counts retained original prompt/output records across all arms, not judging pairs or replay-expanded regression observations. The manipulation's intent-to-treat language concerns incomplete suppression of rewriting, not retention of all assigned participants (pp. 38 and 45–47). Differences are grouped by distinct factual issue or contrast; equivalent wording, alternative valid locators and relocation of the same fact between fields are not counted. In particular, the delay-field prose differs but both forms correctly code immediate assisted production, and both already describe later researcher replay. The reconciliation object is preserved unchanged as the record of the earlier screening stage. The final object records the subsequent correction to S1-O1 question routing and the disposition of all open questions; its challenge counts refer only to problems in the challenge files.

resolved.reason: Use the codebook's single-output quality category for expected target-replication quality; question remains none because this is a fixed-target fidelity task.
